findings.text: §67 bundles two independent deliverables (no orphaned arm tree; a storage failure is not a test failure) and its single negative control falsifies only the second, so the tree-reaping half has no control showing it fails at base

findings.reason: a node can satisfy every case while leaving the retry unimplemented, so the plan's own gate would close a half-built deliverable.
findings.text: the deliverable requires that "a landing refused for that reason is retried on another node" but no case in the done-when measures the retry, the node, or the landing's outcome after it

findings.reason: the endpoint as written is unreachable without a reaper that does not depend on that node being reused, so a worker would either under-build it or invent a mechanism the plan has not weighed.
findings.text: "No landing arm's tree outlives its job on the node it ran on" is contradicted by the remedy in the next sentence, which removes a left tree only "before or when that node next runs a landing arm": a node that never runs another arm keeps its trees indefinitely, which is the incident's own shape (eleven trees from several nodes filling two of them)

findings.reason: the remedy follows from the trees existing, not from how full the node was, so only the severity sentence would tighten; the mechanism stands without the percentage.
findings.text: the severity claim does not follow from the plan's own figures: eleven trees at about 1.6 GB is about 17.6 GB in total, so attributing 93 % and 99 % of two nodes' /tmp to them needs the remaining content of those /tmp filesystems to be under about 10 GB, and no such measurement is cited
